nodes.title: The public site (landing, /promises, /privacy, /help, /leaving, not-found, header, footer) is drawn in Volt night inside K's own scope (.kx + data-klook=volt + data-ktheme=night); no site palette
The landing hero shows the product itself: real captures of Home, the Desk mid-lesson (AI label) and Antariksh, re-taken by tests/prod/r11-site-captures.mjs; no painted or stock art

Public site after the Volt rebuild: 18 views (6 pages x 360/412/1366), 0 below a floor (overflow 0, min text 14 px, no target < 44 px, helplines on every page); before: landing 13 px text at all 3 sizes; every landing image and the game video loaded for a scrolling visitor at 360/412/1366 (6/6)

Landing LCP, lab mid phone (412x915 DPR 2.6, CPU 4x, 1.6 Mbps/150 ms), n=5 each: before median 5068 ms (painted hero, 863 KB page), after 4212 ms (desk.webp 25 KB; the below-the-fold game loop is never the LCP element)
A lime brand mark in the site header: rejected, it would be a second lime element next to the CTA (K's one-volt law); the mark is ink on void

md.decisions:
## dc-r11-site-volt-night
**The public site uses K's tokens through K's own scope; landing.css holds layout only.** `src/app/landing/Site.tsx` `VOLT_NIGHT` puts `.kx` + `data-klook="volt"` + `data-ktheme="night"` on the root of the landing and every `SitePage`; the site imports K's `tokens.css`, `kaksha.css` and `futurist.css` and uses K's components (the chamfered `kx-cta`, `kx-ghost`, `kx-label` `//` eyebrows, `kx-cut`). `tests/r11-site-volt.test.mjs` fails on any colour literal, font host or redefined K token in landing.css, and on `--k-move` (lime) outside K's CTA. Loading and RouteError on the public paths use the same scope (K's tokens are already in the main stylesheet).
**Reverse if:** K's look changes again (the site follows K's scope with no edit) or the owner wants the public site to differ from the app.

## dc-r11-site-hero-real-captures
**The hero, the lesson section and the play section show captures of the real app** (Kaksha dev fixture pages in Volt night at 412x915 DPR 2, the Desk under the Kaksha skin at `work-beat` and `work-your_turn`, and a frame of the games harness's own Antariksh recording), written as 600 px wide webp (23-31 KB) to `public/site/`. Re-take with `node tests/prod/r11-site-captures.mjs` whenever the app's look changes; the site never shows a screen the app does not draw.
**Reverse if:** a capture goes stale against the shipped app (re-take it) or the owner wants motion (a short captured loop) instead of stills.
md.measurements:
## m-r11-site-floors
`tests/prod/r11-site-sheets.mjs` on a production build of base `efc0e721` (before) and of this branch (after), served locally, 6 pages x 360x800 / 412x915 / 1366x768 = 18 views each. After: horizontal overflow 0, smallest visible text 14 px, no link or button under 44 px (inline links in sentences exempt), Childline 1098 and Tele-MANAS 14416 and the AI wording on every page. Before: the landing's smallest text was 13 px at all three sizes. Sheets: `docs/design/round4/build/r11/stream2/{before,after}-*.webp`. Date 2026-10-11. Adult harness, no child.

## m-r11-site-lcp
`tests/prod/r11-site-lcp.mjs`, n = 5 cold loads per build, Playwright Chromium on this container with DevTools emulation (412x915, DPR 2.6, CPU 4x slower, 1.6 Mbps down / 150 ms). Before: median 5068 ms, max 5112 ms, LCP element the painted hero webp. After: median 4212 ms, max 4332 ms (with the game loop added below the fold), LCP element `/site/desk.webp` (preloaded on `/` from index.html). Most of what remains is the app's JavaScript before first render, not the site's files. LAB numbers, not field data. Date 2026-10-11.

The full-page sheets are taken after scrolling the page in steps and requiring every image (complete, naturalWidth > 0) and video (readyState >= 2) to have loaded: 6 of 6 on the landing at 360, 412 and 1366. A full-page shot that never scrolls leaves lazy frames empty (rj-r4-fullpage-shot-lazy).
md.rejected:
## rj-r11-site-lime-brand
A lime (`--k-move`) brand mark in the header was tried and dropped: with the hero's lime CTA it puts two lime elements on the first screen, against K's one-volt law. The mark is `--k-ink` on `--k-void`.
